evals.name: surfaces-first-then-one-owner-each
evals.prompt: Accepted contract: the invoices list gets a filter bar (status, date range) and the matching rows must load without a full page reload. The repository has no conventions file. We are about to implement. Which skills own this stage?
evals.expected_output: The surfaces are named from the contract first (a rendered filter UI, client data loading), then routed: frontend-stack owns everything a person sees and operates. No chart or Postgres surface exists, so dataviz and supabase-postgres-best-practices are recorded as not applicable. The precedence level behind each answer is recorded.
assertions: Names the surfaces the change touches before naming any skill
Routes the visible UI surfaces to frontend-stack
Does NOT route to dataviz or supabase-postgres-best-practices for a change with no chart and no Postgres surface, and records them as not applicable rather than omitting them
Records which precedence level supplied each routing answer
Does NOT give frontend guidance of its own (component structure, styling, motion values)

evals.name: postgres-surface-routes-to-postgres-not-to-the-frontend-index
evals.prompt: Accepted contract: add a tenant_id column to the invoices table, backfill it, add the index the tenant queries need, and tighten the RLS policy so a tenant only sees its own invoices. There is a small admin toggle in the settings page to enable the new policy. Route the implementation stage.
evals.expected_output: Two surfaces: the Postgres schema/RLS/index work goes to supabase-postgres-best-practices; the settings toggle goes to frontend-stack. Neither skill is loaded for the other's surface, and no surface resolves to two skills.
assertions: Routes the schema, backfill, index and RLS work to supabase-postgres-best-practices
Routes the settings toggle to frontend-stack
Does NOT load frontend-stack for the database surface or the Postgres skill for the toggle
Every named surface has exactly one owner

evals.name: repository-conventions-override-the-global-table
evals.prompt: The repository's .claude/knowledge/cases/acme-web/conventions.md contains, under Implementation-pass overrides: '| Postgres queries and migrations | the in-house `acme-db` skill | review round 3, PR #212 |'. The accepted change adds a migration and one query. Route the implementation stage.
evals.expected_output: The repository's override wins: the migration and query are routed to acme-db, with precedence level 2 (repository conventions) recorded as the source. The global routing row for Postgres is not applied and is not copied into the conventions file.
assertions: Routes the migration and query to the repository's acme-db skill, not to supabase-postgres-best-practices
Records that the repository's conventions (precedence level 2) supplied the answer
Does NOT propose copying or restating the global routing rule into conventions.md
Cites the override's provenance (review round 3, PR #212) as what gives it authority

evals.name: two-claimants-are-resolved-by-removal
evals.prompt: Two installed skills both claim to own React component structure: 'vercel-composition-patterns' and a newer 'react-architecture' skill someone added last month. They disagree on compound components. The change touches a component library. How do you resolve the routing?
evals.expected_output: The overlap is resolved by removing one of the two skills, not by declaring a winner that every future reader would have to honour. Loading both is named as a defect. The change proceeds with exactly one owner for the surface.
assertions: Resolves the overlap by removing (uninstalling or retiring) one skill rather than by declaring a winner in prose
Explains that a declared precedence holds only while every reader honours it, while a removal always holds
Does NOT load both skills for the same surface
Ends with exactly one owner for the component-structure surface

evals.name: uncovered-surface-is-owed-not-silent
evals.prompt: Accepted contract: the report page gains a weekly-active-users chart, and the numbers come from a new Postgres materialized view. The dataviz skill is not installed in this environment. Route the implementation stage and emit the stage receipt.
evals.expected_output: Surfaces: the chart, the surrounding page, and the materialized view. dataviz would own the chart and is recorded as unavailable with its coverage owed; frontend-stack takes the surrounding page; supabase-postgres-best-practices takes the view. The receipt separates applied from owed.
assertions: Records dataviz as unavailable with the chart coverage explicitly owed
Does NOT let frontend-stack or a design skill decide the chart form in dataviz's absence
Routes the materialized view to supabase-postgres-best-practices and the surrounding page to frontend-stack
The stage receipt distinguishes skills applied from coverage owed and names every uncovered surface

evals.name: owed-skill-is-looked-up-and-offered-not-installed
evals.prompt: Accepted contract: add a nullable archived_at column to the projects table, a partial index for the non-archived rows, and exclude archived projects from the RLS select policy. The supabase-postgres-best-practices skill is not installed in this environment. We are about to dispatch the implementation stage. Route it.
evals.expected_output: The Postgres surface would be owned by supabase-postgres-best-practices, which is unavailable, so its coverage is owed. Before dispatch the routing looks the owed coverage up (loads find-skills, or names the read-only `npx skills find` search it runs and reports it blocked when it cannot run it), presents what it found or would present, and ends the turn asking the human which package, if any, to install. It installs nothing and does not let another skill cover the surface meanwhile.
assertions: Records supabase-postgres-best-practices as unavailable with the Postgres coverage owed

Looks the owed coverage up before implementation: loads find-skills through the Skill tool, or names the read-only skills search (npx skills find with a query for the surface) and reports the result or that the search could not run
Does NOT install a skill, and does NOT run or instruct running `npx skills add` as something it is doing now
Ends the turn asking the human to decide which found package, if any, to install, instead of proceeding with implementation
States that the coverage stays owed until a skill is actually installed and loaded, not merely found

evals.name: surface-with-no-row-is-looked-up
evals.prompt: Accepted contract: when an invoice is finalized the server renders it as a PDF (logo, line items, totals, page numbers) and stores it in object storage; the invoice page gains a Download PDF button. The repository has no conventions file. Route the implementation stage before it is dispatched.
evals.expected_output: Surfaces: server-side PDF rendering, storage write, and the download button. The button goes to frontend-stack. PDF rendering has no owner in the global table, so it is recorded as uncovered and looked up (find-skills, or the named read-only search) before dispatch; candidates, or the fact the search could not run, are presented and the human decides whether to install. Nothing is installed and no general-purpose skill is stretched over the PDF surface.
assertions: Routes the Download PDF button to frontend-stack
Records server-side PDF rendering as a surface with no covering skill

Looks up coverage for the PDF surface: loads find-skills through the Skill tool, or names the read-only skills search (npx skills find with a PDF-related query) and reports the result or that it could not run
Does NOT install a skill or treat a found candidate as applied coverage
Asks the human whether to install a candidate before the stage is dispatched

evals.name: fully-covered-change-does-not-search
evals.prompt: Accepted contract: the settings page gains a toggle for weekly digest emails, persisted in a new boolean column on the profiles table with a migration. frontend-stack and supabase-postgres-best-practices are both installed. Route the implementation stage.
evals.expected_output: Two surfaces, each with an installed owner: the toggle to frontend-stack, the column and migration to supabase-postgres-best-practices. Nothing is owed, so no skills search runs, find-skills is not loaded, and the routing does not stop to ask about installing anything.
assertions: Routes the toggle to frontend-stack and the column and migration to supabase-postgres-best-practices
Does NOT load find-skills (it does not appear in the skills the agent invoked) and does NOT propose a skills search
Does NOT stop to ask the human about installing skills
Records that nothing is owed

evals.name: dispatched-agent-returns-candidates-without-waiting
evals.prompt: You are the implementation agent that the software factory dispatched for this stage; no human is reachable from this session and your final message goes back to the orchestrator. Accepted contract: the dashboard gains a stacked bar chart of monthly revenue by plan. The dataviz skill is not installed. Route the implementation stage and return your stage receipt.
evals.expected_output: dataviz is unavailable and the chart coverage is owed. Because no human is reachable, the agent does not wait for or address a human and installs nothing; it records the lookup (find-skills or the named search, or that it could not run) and returns the receipt to the orchestrator with the install decision flagged as pending a human, so the loop can stop at its own gate.
assertions: Records dataviz as unavailable with the chart coverage owed
Looks the owed coverage up: loads find-skills through the Skill tool, or names the read-only skills search (npx skills find with a chart-related query) and reports the result or that it could not run
Does NOT install a skill or run `npx skills add`
Returns a stage receipt that explicitly marks the install decision as pending a human (for the orchestrator to take to its gate), and does NOT declare the stage ready to proceed with no blockers
Does NOT pick a substitute charting library or chart form itself to cover the owed surface
